## Intent — what this is for

Traced defect, not a task row. apps/manifest.py:313 claimed of permissions.appMessaging "This is the install-consent surface for who an app can talk to, shown in the Store via to_dict" — true on the server (to_dict emits it, catalog._manifest_consent carries it into the pre-install entry, GET /api/apps returns it) and false at the last mile: AppPermissionsWire (web/src/lib/api.ts) never declared the field and PermissionList never rendered it, so the browser received the targets and dropped them. Measured on the unchanged component with {cron: true, appMessaging: ["receiver", "mail-*"]}: the whole consent output was "Permissions the gateway enforces • Scheduled jobs" plus EI-12 D2's network advisory. Owned here rather than reopened as APE-9 because APE-9's done_when covers the broker only and every clause of it holds — enforcement is real (apps/messaging.py:167 → can_use_app_messaging, 403 + SEL on an undeclared pair); the manifest comment overreached. Discovered during EI-12 D2 and recorded in that plan's log as needing its own atom. NOT the same shape as D2: D2 made network an ADVISORY row because app egress cannot be confined, whereas appMessaging IS enforced and belongs in the enforced bullets beside Storage / Scheduled jobs / Run background agents, uncaveated. Only D2's treatment of silence carries over — declaring no target is stated, not left blank. D2's load-bearing Object.keys(permissions).length > 0 Store-panel guard is untouched.

## Done when

the Store names the apps a declaring app may message, in both surfaces PermissionList serves, among the permissions the gateway ENFORCES; a trailing-* target renders as the name prefix it is (mirroring _matches_any — the grant covers every current and future app under the prefix) and a bare * as any installed app; declaring none is disclosed as messaging no app (deny-by-default) rather than left silent; AppPermissionsWire declares the field and a test pins the server leg end to end (the pre-install catalog payload AND GET /api/apps, not just the component in isolation), backed by a two-sided rail that the wire type declares exactly the keys Permissions.to_dict() can emit; apps/manifest.py's comment is true afterwards. No first-party app declares appMessaging, so the rendering cases are synthetic manifests — stated plainly rather than implied — DONE 2026-08-13 (backend 18956 passed / 0 failed — baseline 18953 + 3 new; web 1832 passed across 192 files + 5 new; tsc + build clean; validated live in an isolated home)
